Graduate Student Stipend & Awards
Admission cannot be granted until a position and financial support has been defined. It is therefore imperative that all graduate students have a firm commitment from a Faculty member for supervision and financial support.
Graduate Student Stipend
Students accepted into the MBB graduate program are guaranteed financial support.
MBB Grad Student Stipend Guidelines - 2025 (PDF)
MBB PhD Minimum Funding Policy - Jan 2024 (PDF)
MBB PhD Funding Policy - FAQ - Aug 2024 (PDF)
Effective Fall 2026 the minimum stipend is $28,500 for MSc students and $30,500 *(+ $5,508 PhD Research Scholarship in years 1-4) for PhD students.
The guaranteed financial support lasts three years for MSc students and five years for PhD students.
Normally, full financial support is typically sourced from scholarships, fellowships, teaching assistantships, and graduate research assistantships, generally requiring that the Supervisor agree to provide a graduate research assistantship for at least one term per year. It is important to discuss your financial assistance expectations with your proposed Supervisor. While holding such support, you are expected to be engaged full time in your course work, research, and teaching duties.
The financial support offered to MBB students does not include tuition and fees.
*The $5,508 PhD Research Scholarship supports new and current research-based PhD students at SFU, as long as they meet all the eligibility requirements and conditions as outlined in these Terms of Reference.
MBB Graduate Scholarships and Awards
Graduate Awards
These award amounts are incorporated into regular MBB graduate stipends, and do not increase base stipend rates. The Graduate Program Assistant announces a competition for these awards, typically, in May.
GRADUATE FELLOWSHIPS (GF)
MBB holds an annual Graduate Fellowship (GF) competition (valued at $7000). Cumulative grade point average (CGPA) requirement is 3.50.
PRESIDENT'S PHD SCHOLARSHIP (PS)
President's PHD Scholarship reward PhD students who have made excellent progress in their degree, completing all university and program requirements. This award is held during or before the student's 12th term. Students who did not complete a Master's program before transferring into a PhD are eligible to hold the award within the first 12 terms of their PhD, from the PhD start date.
Graduate Travel and Research Award (TARA)
The Graduate Travel and Research Award (TARA) is designed to encourage student participation in remote research opportunities or academic conferences. The goal of this program is to generate new travel opportunities for MBB students, facilitating involvement in scientific events that would normally be a significant financial burden for their supervising faculty. This award amount is offered in addition to regular stipend funding.
Value: up to $2,000
Application Deadline: October 20, 2026
Download the 2026-27 MBB TARA Terms of Reference (PDF)
Eligibility
Applicant (Student) Eligibility Requirements:
Must formally participate in the event (e.g., oral or poster presentation at a conference)
Open to both domestic and international students
Open to students supervised by Full, Associate, or Adjunct MBB faculty members
Travel must take place between January 1, 2026 and August 31, 2027. Both past and confirmed future travel are eligible with proof of registration.
During Spring 2027 (the payment term), the student must be:
registered full-time and in good academic standing, and
within 9 terms (3 years) of the start of their MSc program, or within 15 terms (5 years) of the start of their PhD program (for MSc–PhD transfers, term count begins at the first PhD term). Approved leaves do not count toward term limits
May be held only once during a student’s graduate program
Application Process
In a single merged PDF file named "Lastname-TARA.pdf", submit to mbb@sfu.ca, in the following order:
1. Student Submission:
Current CV: please generate and submit a Canadian Common CV
A one-page statement of interest including:
A description of the conference or research activity, with exact travel dates, accomodation details, and the student's role
A description of the anticipated benefits from event participation
The abstract submitted to the event (formatted as required by the conference/host)
A current graduate transcript
2. Supervisor Submission:
A support letter describing the student’s role in the research and what will be presented or undertaken, that is cosigned by the supervisor and student
A budget of expenses (past or projected), prepared jointly with the student
A commitment to cover expenses not funded by TARA
A justification of financial need and/or the significance of the opportunity
Evaluation
Applications will be reviewed by the Scholarship Committee, considering:
evidence of the student's research achievementsjudication Criteria:
Academic impact and educational value of the opportunity (priority will be given to international events or those with large audiences)
Supervisor's financial need (priority may be given to opportunities that would otherwise be prohibitively expensive)
Availability of funds within the TARA budget
Administration note: For travel completed before Spring 2026, supervisors may have already reimbursed student expenses from their research grants. In such cases, the TARA payment will be treated as part of the student’s Spring 2027 stipend (contributing to the departmental minimum stipend guarantee). Supervisors may reduce their stipend contribution in that term by an amount equal to the TARA award.
